{{Short description|Theorem in algebraic geometry}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Lüroth's theorem''' asserts that every [[field (mathematics)|field]] that lies between a field ''K'' and the [[rational function field]] ''K''(''X'') must be generated as an [[field extension|extension]] of ''K'' by a single element of ''K''(''X''). This result is named after [[Jacob Lüroth]], who proved it in 1876.<ref>{{citation|chapter=Lueroth (or Lüroth), Jakob|url=http://www.encyclopedia.com/doc/1G2-2830902699.html|first=Werner |last=Burau|title=Complete Dictionary of Scientific Biography|year=2008}}</ref>

==Statement==
Let <math>K</math> be a field and <math>M</math> be an intermediate field between <math>K</math> and <math>K(X)</math>, for some indeterminate ''X''. Then there exists a [[rational function]] <math>f(X)\in K(X)</math> such that <math>M=K(f(X))</math>. In other words, every
intermediate extension between <math>K</math> and <math>K(X)</math> is a [[simple extension]].

==Proofs==
The proof of Lüroth's theorem can be derived easily from the theory of [[rational curve]]s, using the [[geometric genus]].<ref>{{citation|title=Algebraic Numbers and Algebraic Functions|volume=4|series=Chapman Hall/CRC Mathematics Series|first=P. M.|last=Cohn|author-link=Paul Cohn|publisher=CRC Press|year=1991|isbn=9780412361906|page=148|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=KE4jqiw37PoC&pg=PA148}}.</ref>
This method is non-elementary, but several short proofs using only the basics of [[Field theory (mathematics)|field theory]] have long been known, mainly using the concept of [[transcendence degree]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Lang |first=Serge |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-1-4613-0041-0 |title=Algebra |date=2002 |publisher=Springer New York |isbn=978-1-4612-6551-1 |edition=3rd |series=Graduate Texts in Mathematics |volume=211 |location=New York, NY |pages=355 |chapter=Ch VIII.1 Transcendence bases |doi=10.1007/978-1-4613-0041-0}}</ref>
Many of these simple proofs use [[Gauss's lemma (polynomial)|Gauss's lemma on primitive polynomials]] as a main step.<ref>E.g. see [https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3e/Another_elementary_proof_of_Luroth%27s_theorem-06.2004.pdf this document], or {{citation|title=A Course in Constructive Algebra|series=Universitext |first1=Ray|last1=Mines|first2=Fred|last2=Richman|publisher=Springer|year=1988|isbn= 9780387966403|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fMsdixbW4NoC&pg=PA148|page=148}}.</ref>
